Shell(git add context.md \ src/OpcBridge.App/DashboardPage.cs \ src/OpcBridge.App/Hmi/HmiTagSnapshot.cs \ src/OpcBridge.App/MappingRequests.cs \ src/OpcBridge.App/MappingStore.cs \ src/OpcBridge.App/Program.cs \ src/OpcBridge.Client/HmiTagDto.cs \ src/OpcBridge.Core/TagMapping.cs \ src/OpcBridge.Hmi.Core/MultiBridgeTagCache.cs \ src/OpcBridge.Hmi/OpcBridge.Hmi.csproj \ src/OpcBridge.Hmi/ViewModels/FaceplateViewModel.cs \ tests/OpcBridge.LoadTest/DashboardPageTests.cs \ tests/OpcBridge.LoadTest/HmiApiTests.cs \ tests/OpcBridge.LoadTest/MultiBridgeTagCacheTests.cs \ tests/OpcBridge.LoadTest/TagDigitalTests.cs \ tests/OpcBridge.LoadTest/MappingDigitalApiTests.cs \ && git commit -F - <<'EOF' feat(tags): digital two-state tags with on/off status text Add per-tag Digital / OnText / OffText so a two-state signal renders as operator text ("Running"/"Stopped") instead of a raw value. Digital is tri-state: null = auto (Boolean/Bool tags are digital, anything else analog), true = force digital, false = force analog. Byte and other numeric tags stay analog until marked because a 0-255 flag is indistinguishable from a real analog counter by type, and a value-based guess would flip at runtime. - TagDigital (OpcBridge.Core) resolves the mode and coerces values to a boolean ("non-zero = on"), covering CLR primitives, strings and JsonElement since live HMI values arrive as JSON. - Plumbing: TagMapping -> MappingTagDto/ToTagMapping -> MappingStore, config import/export -> HmiTagSnapshot -> HmiTagDto -> MultiBridgeTagEntry. - FaceplateViewModel.FormatDigital renders the label, falling back to the raw value when no label is configured. Faceplate-only by design: trends, widgets and the tag browser keep raw values. - Dashboard: faceplate Digital/On text/Off text fields, a session-scoped 0/1 observation that surfaces a "0/1?" hint on the Maps row (nothing is ever marked automatically), and updateMapping echoes the fields because POST /api/mappings/update is a full replace. Co-authored-by: CommandCodeBot <noreply@commandcode.ai> EOF)

Shell(git add src/OpcBridge.Hmi/Services/LocalBridgeDetector.cs tests/OpcBridge.LoadTest/BridgeRowTests.cs \ && git commit -F - <<'EOF' fix(hmi): probe container-published bridge host ports A bridge running in a container is reachable on the published host port (docker run -p 18080:8080), never on its own self-reported 8080-8180 range, so scanning that range could not find it. BuildDefaultCandidates() now tries the standard local URLs, then the documented publish ports (KnownHostPorts), then the scan range. Known ports come first because the range can contain ports that accept a connection but never answer, each costing a full probe timeout. Co-authored-by: CommandCodeBot <noreply@commandcode.ai> EOF)
